questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the university offered interesting courses I couldn't get at my home university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Universtiy of Iceland was great! Nice city, good teaching, interesting courses, and nice accomodation. However, there were some trouble with getting my courses approved by the university of Iceland, not letting me have the courses I originally wanted

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Due to COVID, there was only a single zoom meeting anc the guided tour around campus did not give me the information I needed. It lasted less than 5 minutes, and I still didn't know where neither classroom or library was.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were several student housings on campus and in the city. The wait lists were long and nothing was guaranteed, but most students were able to find accomodation here.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We were 9 people who shared a double kitchen

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's great - nice people and parties (unless COVID). Good soundproofing, so it was quite during the night. There are, however, no linens, duvet or pillow when you arrive

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I believe it all went through mobility online, and a formal application. No big problems

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I was always able to contact the person in charge exchange students at the university of Iceland, who answered quickly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had some problems because I was automatically enrolled in a rather narrow faculty. University of Iceland required me to take 60% of my ECTS within this faculty, which later on was proven not to be accepted by KU. The ECTS scores for each course also varied, why it was rather difficult getting the courses to an even 30 ECTS

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't settle! I think both HI and KU, and especially HI, would give some wiggle room if I would've argued my case a bit more

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The general level was proven to be a bit lower than at KU

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Quite similar, although we had 4 courses at once throughout the whole semester instead of "blok struktur". Otherwise it consisted mainly of lecturers and a few practical sessions where we were to give presentations and discussions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Natural Hazards
Marine Environment and Fisheries
Ecology B
Critical Use and Representation of Geographic Information
The Arctic Circle

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Marine environment and fisheries! Our teacher, Freydis, was fairly new to the teaching game and had so much to give. She was enthustiastic, the topic were interesting, and she arranged guest lecturers with people in the industry / researcers to give insight to what one can work with

questions.answer: Additional travel insurance

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive, and beers, food and generally nights out

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was able to find a student organization within my subject due to an coincidence. However, there were very little information about this from the University, and almost no clubs, groups, etc. arranged by the University. Most was done on initiative by the students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Choir, student organizations, exchange student groups

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Student organizations! They exist, you just have to find them, and they arrange all kinds of social activities from parties, hikes, bathing tours, book clubs, etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hot springs, public swimming pool, hike (Mount Esja), and of course travel! See the country! Most students were travelling in the south coast, the westfjords if possible, Vestmannaeyjar (!!), the North (Akureyri, Husavik - here you can go whale watching) and Snæfellsnes.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, the culture is similar to the one back home, although they are way more relaxed at easy-going.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Student organizations!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Icelanders are very easy-going and have an expression for "We'll see", meaning that plans were difficult to plan ahead and you mainly made plans the same day.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Same as descriped above - although challenging at first, once you get the drift it's quite nice

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Join a student organization
Explore the country
Relax - it'll be find. Icelanders are very easy-going and flexible, and they're extremely helpful

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Hmm

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making new friends from other countries

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Group work with people from different cultures, and living away from my friends and safe space back home

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
